subtype: Approach: prepares a backup for the likely thing that could go wrong [Action]
passage: Sit, Vaibhav. You want to know why I always carry two tickets? Let me tell you what Yash did at twenty. December, a banking exam in Lucknow, and every newspaper full of fog. I booked the night train, but I also went to the bus stand and bought a seat for later that night, and wrote both timings inside my ticket folder: train at nine, bus at eleven if the train failed. My friends laughed. The train was five hours late. Half the platform sat on their bags staring at the empty tracks. I opened my folder, walked to the bus stand and caught the last bus. I reached the city at dawn with time to wash my face. Two tickets cost me a little. Missing that exam would have cost me a year.

qa.q: What did Yash write inside the ticket folder?
qa.a: Yash wrote both timings there: train at nine, bus at eleven if the train failed.

qa.q: How did Yash probably feel when the train ran five hours late?
qa.a: Yash was probably worried but relieved, because the folder already had the bus timing ready.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story kept the exam from being missed?
qa.a: Buying the bus seat and noting both timings beforehand meant Yash could switch at once when the train failed.

qa.q: How might the other people on the platform have felt?
qa.a: They may have felt stuck and anxious, sitting on their bags without a backup like the one Yash had.

grounding: Shows a student booking a bus alongside a train and noting timings in case fog delays the train.
